links.note: Asks the functions of parties; the model answer opens 'fill political offices and exercise political power' and its first numbered point is 'Contest elections ... by putting up their candidates'. 24093 is the entry and principal function; 24094 (making laws/running government) and 24095 (opinion/welfare access) are the later functions the same answer continues into.

Asks the challenges parties face; the answer's leading and longest point is 'Lack of internal democracy ... organisational meetings are not held, members are not consulted'. 24102 (dynastic succession, money and muscle) is the sibling challenge that follows, not the one the answer opens on.

Asks explicitly for reforms to strengthen parties; answer lists regulating internal affairs, elections from lower tier upward, maintaining a register. That is 24103 Reform measures, not 24101 which states the defect rather than the remedy.

Straight definition question, and the answer is the definition verbatim: 'a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in the government ... agree on some policies and programmes'. 24090's description is that sentence.

Characteristics, and the answer's distinguishing items are 'definite views on various issues', 'a general ideological identity ... leftist or rightist', 'it represents a part of society'. That is partisanship and ideology (24091), not the bare definition (24090, which qid:87514 tests) and not the leaders/members/followers triad (24092).
Fill-in of the definition itself; the stem is 24090's description word for word and the answer is 'political party'.

Three of the four pairs are party-to-alliance (Congress-UPA, BJP-NDA, CPI(M)-Left Front); those three alliances are the worked example of the multi-party system in the text. 24099 National parties would fit a question naming the parties' recognition criteria, which this does not; only the fourth pair (TDP-State party) touches 24100.

BSP's founder Kanshi Ram is recall from the national-parties roster, where each recognised national party is listed with its founder. A name-recall item still sits inside the concept the name belongs to, which here is 24099, not a generic one.

'Integral humanism' is the BJP's stated guiding philosophy as given in the national-parties roster. 24091 Partisanship and ideology is about a party being known by its ideology in general; this item is recall of one named national party's entry.

The key is (b) A and B, so what discriminates is that statement C, 'parties are not necessary to run governments', is false. That is the necessity-of-parties point in 24088 (parties became necessary as democracies expanded). A and B are merely the chapter's opening remark on popular distrust.

The Yunus passage turns on his party being 'democratic from the grassroots level' and 'different from the traditional ones', and sub-question (c) asks how to organise it differently. That contrast is internal democracy (24101). 24103 Reform measures is the sibling but covers the statutory instruments (anti-defection law, affidavits, Election Commission), none of which the passage raises.
